# A11-S07: La Stampa article

Correspondence extract. Omissions are marked […].

[…]

Artificial intelligence: cross and delight of a humanity by now on its way
on the road (without return?) of posthumanism. And with the impression that the
the march in that direction happens at an ever faster pace. The news
of the last stage burned in matter comes not from California –
the outpost of the *post-human* – but from the Old Continent; and for the
precision from the country where William Shakespeare had placed the pressing
ontological questions of Hamlet. In fact, from Copenhagen there arrives
the announcement of participation in the next political elections (in
June 2023) of the Synthetic Party, hopeful to gather support
sufficient to make their entrance into the Folketing, the Parliament
Danish unicameral. Strong in its peculiarity: the nature of the formation
*Data-driven* and algorithmic politics, with a program drawn up by a
artificial intelligence system. Main target the 15% of 
citizens-voters who, in the general consultation of 2019, are
retreated into abstention, providing cause for concern for a
a nation accustomed to thinking of itself, even in the metamorphoses of postmodernity,
as a cradle of civic virtues and popular participation in life
public. To intercept them, programs from all 
 have been collectedminor party organizations of the Country from 1970 to our days, and
The AI has produced an overall platform that should thus meet
the approval of the disappointed and the abstainers who did not feel
represented by the existing political offer. An electoral program
therefore capable of presenting "the political visions of the person
common," as assert the current leaders of the Synthetic Party who
coincide with the members of an artistic collective, Computer Lars – animated
when Asker Bryld Staunaes, [████] and Valentin Louis
Georges Eugène Marcel Proust (a pseudonym, a program...), – which is the
project manager, indeed, of the "Synthetic Party project" at 
the Danish high-tech company MindFuture. Not by chance, also on the lexical level
we find ourselves very far from the most traditional political language (and
umanistico): and, in fact, Det Syntetiske Parti is to be considered as a mix
of protest against the political class, original proposal-recipe (inserted
in the widespread context of the succeeding Algorithm Society, in line with
continuity, to that of networks) and provocation. Birthed by a group of
artists of a country that has experienced seasons of artistic avant-gardism of
rupture (from the Co.Bra Movement to the Situationist International), and that,
in addition to having a history of postmaterialist political values,
youth protest, libertarianism and *hacking* – like all the
Scandinavia – it is on the frontier of experiments in relations
between politics and technology (as already happened in the case of the «Partito dei
pirates"). Between criticism of political elites and the centrality of the *common
people*, an *Ai-driven* spirit hovers over the training
technopopulism. By virtue of which, any function having been archived
political pedagogy, work is carried out according to the scheme, already used
currently, of the reproposal to the electorate of what they want to hear
say, with the amplification and refinement in terms of “firepower”
guaranteed by artificial intelligence.

The positivists of the nineteenth century theorized a "positive politics",
guided by science and technology. Now big data, behavioral
sciences, *computational social science* (which shifts the focus from
understanding to prediction of attitudes and behaviors),
*computational
politics*, neuroscience, platformization of public opinion and,
above all, AI make possible the fulfillment of their dream (or
distopia). And it is an irony of fate that the first “computational
party” is founded by irreverent artists. Waiting for Hal 9000 and
associates to take care of themselves...

[…]
